sheet-1.description: Sheet 1 lies at the southeast corner of Belleville along the Newark city line, where the Second River is crossed by a stone and concrete bridge at Washington Avenue and Broadway. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies toward the upper right. The left third of the page is the Newark side of the river, marked 'Newark Volume Four', with a veterinary hospital, a dairy and a large vacant and open one-story factory building shown only in outline. Belleville lies to the right of the river. A strip of Essex County Belleville Park Commission land borders the river, and Mill Street runs along its edge past long deep lots with scattered frame dwellings and garages (block 116). A group of auto sales and service buildings with a private garage stands on the north side of Washington Avenue at Mill Street. Cleveland Street runs diagonally from Dow Street down to Quinton Street and Schuyler Street, separating the blocks between it and Van Rensselaer Street (block 117), which hold small frame dwellings with garages, a filling station and a few brick-veneered or concrete-floored outbuildings. South of Washington Avenue are further lots, a machine shop and apartments on Mill Street, and detached frame houses along Quinton Street. At the bottom the Erie Railroad Newark Branch crosses the sheet on a steel bridge over the river, with the Cleveland Street Station, an express station and a freight building beside the tracks. Water mains are lettered in the streets. Adjoining sheets are 44 to the north, 3 to the east and 2 to the south.
notes: Van Rensselaer is Van Renselaer Street today (one s fewer).
Mill, Dow, Cleveland, Quinton and Schuyler are Mill Street, Dow Street, Cleveland Street, Quinton Street and Schuyler Street today.
Clark is Clark Terrace today.
The left part of the sheet is the City of Newark, marked 'Newark Volume Four'; the river name could not be read with certainty (Second River).

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 shows the south-eastern corner of Belleville along the Passaic River, at 50 feet to an inch, turned so that north points to the right of the page (about 75 degrees). It runs from Mill Street and the Erie Railroad Newark Branch at the top down to the Passaic River shore, with Cortlandt, Terrace Place and Main crossing it and Schuyler and Bayard running across them; a stream (the Second River) runs down the left edge with a concrete bridge carrying Main across it. Industry dominates: A. J. Crowhurst and Sons Inc., manufacturers of patent leathers, occupy a large group of beam houses, tanning, colouring and splitting rooms on the river bank; the Hanlon and Goodman Co. paint brush factory and the Viking Tool and Machine Corporation, makers of vending machine machinery, stand south of Main; and Wallace and Tiernan and Co. Inc., manufacturers of chlorine control and chemical feed devices, fill most of the block between Terrace Place and Main with a long factory building, and have a chemical laboratory near the river. Their entry notes that admittance and plans were refused and data came from a previous map and observation. A coal yard with a trestle and a planing mill and lumber sheds lie along the railroad at the top. Frame dwellings line Cortlandt, Terrace Place and Schuyler. An Essex County Park Commission tract and a boat house and club lie on the river front. The Town of Kearny, Hudson County, lies across the river.
notes: Mill is Mill Street, Cortlandt is Cortlandt Street, Schuyler is Schuyler Street, Main is Main Street and Bayard is Bayard Street today.
Terrace Place is drawn ending at Schuyler; the Wallace and Tiernan factory covers the ground beyond.
Main is labelled 100 ft wide at Bayard.
Passaic River front at Main St, Mill St, Cortlandt, Schuyler, Bayard; Wallace & Tiernan, A.J. Crowhurst tannery; north to the right. Bayard/Cortlandt and Bayard/Main hand-picked (boundary street).

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the commercial centre of Belleville where Washington Avenue crosses William Street, between Belleville Avenue at the top and Van Rensselaer Street at the bottom. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about nine degrees, with north toward the upper left. Washington Avenue, a wide street carrying lettered water mains, runs down the middle of the page. Along it stand continuous rows of brick and frame stores with dwellings above (marked S), a bank and a telegraph office near Belleville Avenue, a cinder-block and tile-faced building, a bakery with ovens, a sign and printing works and a group of welding and tile shops. West of Washington Avenue, Washington Street runs parallel between blocks 120 and 122 with small frame dwellings and garages. The Eastwood Hose and Hook and Ladder Company No. 1 fire department and the fire alarm headquarters stand on William Street, and a large printing works and a one-story factory occupy the blocks on either side of Howard Place. Apartment buildings, plumbing shops and filling stations are scattered through the blocks. East of Washington Avenue, Greenwich Street and Valley Street cut off block 73 and block 67, the latter largely open with a few sheds and vacant buildings, bounded by the Erie Railroad Newark Branch near the right edge. Dow Street, Quinton Street and Lincoln Terrace appear at the edges. Adjoining sheets are 8 and 9 to the north, 4 to the east and 2 to the south.
notes: Washington Street and Washington Avenue are both lettered; today they are Washington Street and Washington Avenue.
William, Greenwich, Valley, Dow and Quinton are William Street, Greenwich Street, Valley Street, Dow Street and Quinton Street today.
Van Rensselaer is Van Renselaer Street today.
Valley Street / William Street and Greenwich Street / William Street were detected 9 to 14 m off the fit and left out of the georeferencing.
Washington Av / William centre; Belleville Av, Washington St, Greenwich, Valley, Howard Pl, Dow; Valley/William rejected (rail in Valley); 50 ft

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 shows the east side of Belleville along the Passaic River, between Belleville Avenue at the top and Bayard Street at the bottom, and between Valley Street at the left edge and the river on the right. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about ten degrees, with north toward the upper left. A strip of Essex County Park Commission land follows the river bank, and the town and county line between Belleville in Essex County and Kearny in Hudson County runs along the water. William Street crosses the middle of the page, and Cortlandt Street and Stephens Street run north to Belleville Avenue. The northern blocks (blocks 15 and 12) hold frame dwellings and garages, and the Methodist Episcopal church cemetery and a hall lie at the top near the river. A large apartment building with frame attic stands near the park strip. The Town of Belleville Department of Public Works garage with a miscellaneous storage building lies at the left on William Street, beside the Erie Railroad Newark Branch. South of William Street the Napier Hat Manufacturing Company occupies the corner at Main Street with factory buildings, felt and hat shops, a boiler room, a drying and storage building and a watchman's note giving power, heat and fuel details. South of it stretches the open Christ Episcopal Church Cemetery with a vacant building, and the Tuscarora Canoe Club and boat houses stand at the river edge below Bayard Street. Small shops, a furniture and tile works and dwellings fill the blocks at the left. Adjoining sheets are 9 and 10 to the north and 2 to the south.
notes: Valley, Cortlandt, Stephens, William, Main and Bayard are Valley Street, Cortlandt Street, Stephens Street, William Street, Main Street and Bayard Street today.
The right margin is lettered 'See Map of Harrison-Kearny'.
Valley Street / William Street, with the Erie Railroad Newark Branch beside Valley Street, was detected 4 m off the fit and excluded.
Belleville Av to Bayard, river side; Napier Hat Mfg Co.; Valley/William excluded (Erie Newark Branch in Valley); 50 ft

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers a residential district of central Belleville south of Holmes Street, bounded on the west by Union Avenue and on the east by Hornblower Avenue, with De Witt Avenue running north-south through the middle. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about thirteen degrees, with north toward the upper left. Lloyd Place and Van Houten Place cross the sheet from De Witt Avenue to Hornblower Avenue, and Prospect Place and Academy Street enter at the bottom right. The blocks (numbered 200, 197, 193, 194 and 191) hold detached frame dwellings, most with small garages, and a few of brick or tile. A private convalescent home stands on Holmes Street near Hornblower Avenue. The west half of the page, between Union Avenue and De Witt Avenue south of Lloyd Place, has large deep lots with scattered houses, sheds, a dairy building and garages, and many lots are left blank. Lot lines and house numbers are marked along every frontage, and several corners at Hornblower Avenue are drawn with rounded kerbs. Water mains are lettered in the streets, including 24 and 48 inch mains of the City of Newark and Town of Kearny supplies along Holmes Street and De Witt Avenue. Fire alarm boxes stand at the top left and at Academy Street. Adjoining sheets are 13 to the north, 47 to the west, 7 to the east and 6 to the south.
notes: Holmes and Academy are Holmes Street and Academy Street today.
De Witt Avenue is De Witt Avenue today (two words).
Holmes to Prospect Pl, Union Av to Hornblower Av; 50 ft

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers a residential district in the south of central Belleville, between Union Avenue on the west and Hornblower Avenue on the east and ending at Belleville Avenue at the bottom. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about twelve degrees, with north toward the upper left. Long narrow blocks run north-south between Union Avenue, De Witt Avenue, Prospect Place and Hornblower Avenue (blocks 194 and 191). Most lots hold a detached frame dwelling of two or two and a half stories with a small garage at the rear, drawn in yellow; the west block between Union Avenue and De Witt Avenue has many open lots. Near the bottom left, along Belleville Avenue, stand a one-story garage with a capacity of 30 cars, a restaurant, auto houses and a few dwellings. Academy Street enters from the right at the top, and Rutgers Street ends at Hornblower Avenue near the right edge. Along the bottom edge Belleville Avenue is crossed by Clinton Street, Smith Street and Bridge Street, which continue on sheet 45 below. Water mains are lettered in the streets, including a 24 inch main of the City of Newark supply on De Witt Avenue. Fire alarm boxes stand at Academy Street and at the lower left. Adjoining sheets are 5 to the north, 47 to the west, 8 to the east and 45 to the south.
notes: Academy, Rutgers, Clinton, Smith and Bridge are Academy Street, Rutgers Street, Clinton Street, Smith Street and Bridge Street today.
Georeferenced from six junctions along the right and bottom edges only; the Union Avenue side has no detected control (low confidence there).

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 shows the district around Belleville Public High School in central Belleville, between Holmes Street at the top and Academy Street at the bottom, and from Hornblower Avenue on the west to Washington Avenue on the east. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about eleven degrees, with north toward the upper left. Prospect Street and High Street run north-south between the blocks, and Van Houten Place crosses the middle of the page. The Belleville Public High School occupies the northeast block (block 126) beside Washington Avenue, drawn in brown with an auditorium and gymnasium with balcony, a cafeteria and kitchen, and notes on the dates of its additions (built 1927 and 1928); a smaller store stands next to it. South of Van Houten Place, an Elks lodge (B.P.O.E. Club No. 1123) with an auditorium stands near Washington Avenue, with a bank and a filling station along the avenue, and Wesley M.E. Church stands at the corner of Academy Street at the lower right. The remaining blocks (130, 128 and 125) hold rows of detached frame dwellings of two and two and a half stories with garages, with a few open lots. Lot lines and house numbers are shown along the frontages, and water mains, including a 48 inch main of the Town of Kearny supply, are lettered in the streets. Adjoining sheets are 14 to the north, 5 to the west, 11 to the east and 8 to the south.
notes: Prospect and High are Prospect Street and High Street today; Holmes and Academy are Holmes Street and Academy Street.
The Washington Avenue junctions at Holmes Street and Van Houten Place fit 3.6 and 4.3 m off the other control; Washington Avenue is drawn 100 feet wide.
High School block; Holmes to Academy, Hornblower Av to Washington Av; 50 ft

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the blocks between Hornblower Avenue on the west and Washington Avenue on the east, from Academy at the top to Belleville Avenue at the bottom, in central Belleville, with Rutgers crossing the middle of the sheet. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 11 degrees, with north toward the upper left. The upper half is Block 124, a deep block holding a row of frame dwellings along Academy, the Belleville Public Library (a pink-coloured brick building near the Washington Avenue corner of Academy), a few detached dwellings along Washington Avenue, and, between High and Washington Avenue, Rutgers Hall Apartments, a large pink-coloured brick building of E plan with garages and a filling station beside it. The centre of the block is mostly open lots with lot lines only. High is a short street entering from Rutgers. The lower half holds Blocks 123 and 121, separated by Lincoln Terrace: frame dwellings with small garages face Hornblower Avenue, Lincoln Terrace and Belleville Avenue, a larger garage building stands near Belleville Avenue, and the right-hand block has a few large detached houses facing Washington Avenue. Dow and a second street lettered Washington are stubs at the bottom edge. Water mains are marked in the streets, with fire alarm boxes and telephone and distribution hydrants at several corners. Adjoining sheets are 7 to the north, 6 to the west, 9 to the east and 3 and 45 to the south.
notes: Rutgers is Rutgers Street, Academy is Academy Street, and Belleville Avenue and Hornblower Avenue keep their names today.
High is a short street between Academy and Rutgers on the sheet; in OpenStreetMap that line is Rutgers Court.
The street at the bottom lettered Washington (south of Belleville Avenue) is Washington Street today; Washington Avenue is the wide street at the right.
The modern Rutgers Street / Washington Avenue junction is 12 m from the drawn one and was rejected by the detector; the drawn Washington Avenue bends there.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers an industrial and commercial strip of central Belleville between Washington Avenue on the west and Cortlandt on the east, from Academy at the top to Belleville Avenue at the bottom, crossed in the middle by Rutgers. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 9 degrees, with north toward the upper left. A railroad lettered Erie R.R. (Newark Br.) runs from top to bottom through the centre of the sheet, crossing Academy, Rutgers and Belleville Avenue at grade; a gate house stands beside the track at Academy. West of the railroad, Blocks 75 and 74 hold, along Washington Avenue, frame dwellings, an auto sales and service building and used-car lot; towards the railroad stand a woodworking shop, an auto repair shop, a plumbing shop, a private garage, and the Essex Engine and Machine Corporation works, a group of machine, pattern and erecting shops with its own power and heating plant. The Belleville Town Hall, in brown colour for a frame building, stands near the Belleville Avenue and Washington Avenue corner. East of the railroad, Blocks 72 and 71 are occupied by two large works: Sweeney Lithograph Co., Inc., at the top, and the Overman Cushion Tire Co., Inc., manufacturers of rubber tires, in a large brick building with curing, calender, mixing, boiler and drying departments and a side track from the railroad. Frame dwellings fill the remainder of Block 72 along Rutgers. Water mains of 6 and 8 inches are lettered in the streets. Adjoining sheets are 8 to the west, 10 to the east, 11 to the north and 3 and 4 to the south.
notes: The railroad through the centre is lettered E.R.R. (Newark Br.), the Erie Railroad Newark Branch; the modern map has Valley Street along its line.
Cortlandt is Cortlandt Street and Rutgers is Rutgers Street today.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers the eastern edge of Belleville along the Passaic River, from Cortlandt on the west to the river and the Kearny and North Arlington boundary on the east. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 9 degrees, with north toward the upper left. Academy crosses the upper part of the sheet and Rutgers the middle, running out to the Belleville Turnpike steel bridge over the Passaic River; Belleville Avenue runs along the bottom edge. Stephens and Ralph run north from Academy and Rutgers, and Main, a wide street lettered 100 feet and 60 feet, runs diagonally along the east side next to the Essex County Park Commission land that borders the river. West of Stephens stand a large brick public school in Block 17, and the Overman Cushion Tire Co., Inc. tire warehouse and machine shop in Block 16. East of Stephens the blocks hold a lacquer woodworks, a lumber shed, a sheet metal works, dwellings with garages and a filling station. South of Rutgers is a cemetery with the Belleville Reformed Church and its parish house, and frame dwellings and garages facing Main. The river, the town and county limit between Belleville and Kearny, and the borough line of North Arlington (Bergen County) are lettered along the right edge. A note directs the reader to the map of Harrison and Kearny. Adjoining sheets are 9 to the west, 12 to the north and 4 to the south.
notes: Main is Main Street today, but its modern line does not follow the drawn street at the right; it and the junctions east of Stephens were left out of the fit.

The Cortlandt / Rutgers control point is carried from sheet 9, where the junction is drawn more fully.

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 covers the blocks between Washington Avenue on the west and Stephens on the east, from Holmes at the top to Academy at the bottom, in central Belleville. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 18 degrees, with north toward the upper left. The Erie Railroad Newark Branch (E.R.R., lettered Newark Branch) runs down the middle beside Valley, with several tracks and a side track serving the factories on its east side. West of the railroad Block 77 holds the commercial frontage of Washington Avenue: small shops, a restaurant, an undertaker, the New Jersey Bell Telephone Co. exchange building (the Belleville Exchange, a fireproof structure), a loft building, the Betty-Ross Apartments and the Belleville Post Office. East of the railroad stand the large works of Block 76, the Great Atlantic and Pacific Tea Co. laundry and repair building at the top, a machine shop and, below, the Weidmann paper warehouse and paper-core factory with coal bins and storage tanks. East of Cortlandt, Block 23 holds frame dwellings, garages and, at the top, a Baptist church and a vacant building, backing on Stephens. Van Houten Place enters Washington Avenue at the left. Water mains and a 48 inch main of the Town of Kearny supply are lettered at the top. Adjoining sheets are 7 to the west, 12 to the east, 15 to the north and 9 and 10 to the south.
notes: Holmes is Holmes Street, Academy is Academy Street, Cortlandt is Cortlandt Street, Stephens is Stephens Street and Valley is Valley Street today.
Valley, beside the Erie Railroad Newark Branch, was left out of the control because the railroad runs in it.
Washington Avenue is drawn 100 feet wide; the config sets street_widths.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 covers the strip of Belleville between Stephens on the west and the Passaic River frontage on the east, from Holmes at the top to Academy at the bottom. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 18 degrees, with north toward the upper left. Ralph runs north and south down the middle of the sheet. West of Ralph, Block 22 holds a long row of frame dwellings with small garages facing Stephens and Ralph, and, near the top, the Little Zion U.A.M.E. Church; a machine shop, an ice house, a chemical storage building and a brush factory are drawn among them. East of Ralph, Block 21 is mostly open land with lot lines, with a short row of dwellings at the lower left facing Ralph and, in the lower centre, the Metal Reflector and Flood Light Factory, a long one-storey building with skylights, and smaller brick buildings and a garage at its east end. Main, a wide street, runs along the right side of the blocks beside the Essex County Park Commission land, with the Passaic River and the Town and County limits between Belleville and the Boro of North Arlington, Bergen County, drawn on the right. A 48 inch water main of the Town of Kearny supply crosses at Holmes. Adjoining sheets are 11 to the west, 13 to the north-west, 16 to the north, 10 to the south and 20 to the east.
notes: Holmes is Holmes Street, Academy is Academy Street and Ralph is Ralph Street today.
Main is Main Street today, but its modern line is displaced from the drawn street, so it was left out of the control.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 shows an industrial and mixed-use strip of Belleville between Joralemon on the north and Holmes on the south, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 16 degrees. Washington Avenue runs down the west edge, Valley follows the Erie Railroad Newark Branch through the middle of the sheet, and Cortlandt and Stephens bound the eastern blocks. The west side of Valley is lined with small commercial and automotive uses: the Capitol Movies theatre with an entrance wing, used auto sales, an upholsterer, auto sales and service garages, a filling station with car wash, a bicycle repair shop, tire sales and dwellings with garages. Between Valley and Cortlandt stand the plants of the Isolantite Co. of America Inc., manufacturers of insulating materials, the Thomson Machine Company, makers of bakers machinery, a brass foundry, lumber sheds and the Daniel Mellis lumber and mill works with its planing mill, and, at the south end facing Holmes, the A. M. Leacock Co., makers and repairers of electrical appliances, and a china and glassware decorating works. These factories are drawn with the watchman, heat, power and fire-pail notes of Sanborn industrial plans. East of Cortlandt, between it and Stephens, the Rafter Machine Co. occupies the north end and the remainder is dwellings with garages, with a few small shops. Water mains of six and twelve inches and the 48 inch main of the Town of Kearny supply are marked along the streets. sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 covers the eastern edge of Belleville along the Passaic River, between Joralemon on the north and Holmes on the south, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 17 degrees. Stephens forms the west side of the sheet, Ralph runs down the middle and Main lies along the east side of the built-up blocks. East of Main a broad strip is lettered Essex County Park Commission and is left blank except for two outbuildings, and beyond it the Passaic River is drawn with its winding shore, a compass rose and the dash-dot boundary line between Essex County and the Borough of North Arlington, Bergen County, with a note to see the map of Harrison and Kearny. The blocks between Stephens and Ralph are mostly one and two storey frame dwellings with rear garages. At the north end on Joralemon stand a private garage for trailer trucks of brick and steel construction and a steam laundry. Between Ralph and Main are dwellings, a dry cleaning shop, an insecticide factory, a wire cloth factory and a food packer's building of concrete and brick, while the southern third of these blocks is largely vacant land with a few dwellings, a store and a miscellaneous storage shed facing Holmes. The sheet carries six and twelve inch water mains in the streets and the 48 inch main of the Town of Kearny supply along the foot of the sheet. South of the tracks the Essex Lumber & Coal Co. Inc. occupies the block along the railroad with building material, lumber and coal sheds on a trestle siding, and beside it stands the large Fruit Products Corp. cherry bottling plant, with cooking, glace, packing and bottling departments. Cortlandt separates this yard from a row of detached dwellings, and the block between Cortlandt and Stephens holds dwellings, garages, a laundry and a research laboratory. Terry bounds the sheet on the east. The block at the foot of the sheet, beyond Stephens, belongs to sheet 31. Water mains of six and twelve inches are marked in the streets. sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 69 degrees, continuing sheet 17 to the east, so that Washington Avenue runs across the top and Terry and Little run down the page. sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 70 degrees, continuing sheet 18 to the east, with Washington Avenue across the top and Little down the left side. Along Washington Avenue a row of stores and automobile businesses fills the frontage between Little and Overlook Avenue: used auto sales, auto sales and service buildings with repair shops, a bakehouse, dwellings and small stores, all behind a continuous street line. South of the tracks the block between Little, Cortlandt and the streets at the east edge is nearly empty, with a few dwellings on Little and a single large concrete building at the centre marked vacant and open. A second block between Cortlandt and Stephens holds dwellings along Little, a garage and storehouse for doors and a few sheds, and is otherwise open lots. sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 shows a residential district of Belleville laid out as four long blocks between Union Avenue on the north and Linden Avenue on the south, with Joralemon forming the western edge and Division Avenue the eastern edge. Union Avenue, an 80 foot street, bounds the sheet along the top, Linden Avenue along the bottom, Division Avenue along the left and Little Street along the right; Tappan Avenue and Malone Avenue run the length of the sheet between them, and De Witt Avenue crosses the middle. sheet-29.description: Sheet 29 covers the Greylock Avenue and Roosevelt Avenue strip along the east edge of Belleville, between Washington Avenue at the top and Main Street at the bottom, with the Passaic River and the North Arlington boundary on the right. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 74 degrees, so that north lies toward the upper right; the compass rose is at the left. Greylock Avenue and the parallel Roosevelt Avenue run down the page with narrow lots of small frame dwellings, many with garages, and a few brick-veneered buildings and a laundry on the west side near Ralph. At the top, Greylock Parkway meets Greylock Avenue and Washington Avenue, and the blocks on Railroad Place are built up with dwellings; the Erie Railroad (Newark Branch) crosses the sheet just below them, between Railroad Place and Riverdale Avenue. sheet-30.description: Sheet 30 covers the industrial strip along the east edge of Belleville beside the Passaic River, from Washington Avenue at the top to Main Street and River Road at the bottom, with the Nutley boundary on the right. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 74 degrees, so north lies toward the upper right; the compass rose is at the top right. Two large works dominate. At upper left the Westinghouse Electric and Manufacturing Company, Westinghouse Lamp Division (Belleville Plant), makers of radio and incandescent lamp bases, fills the blocks along the north side of the Erie Railroad's Newark Branch with a series of brick factory buildings, a press machine shop and a glass manufacturing and mixing department. Beyond King Street and Hancox Avenue the L. Sonneborn Sons plant (paints, varnish and oil) occupies a long series of buildings, drum storage yards, and a varnish factory. The Federal Leather Company, makers of artificial leather, holds the large block near the bottom, with coating machine, finishing, drying and storage buildings drawn in blue as fire-resistive construction, and a doping division and mixing houses near Main Street. Open land, high-tension transmission lines of the Public Service Electric and Gas Company, and the Nutley boundary line cross the sheet. At the bottom the Passaic River and the Bergen County boundary appear, and the lower right is marked as the map of Harrison-Kearny. Water pipes, watchman notes and fire-protection details are given for each plant.
notes: Cramer Avenue is Carmer Avenue today, and King is King Street.

sheet-31.description: Sheet 31 covers the eastern edge of Belleville between Mansion Place at the top and Joralemon Street at the bottom, from Stephens Street on the west to the Passaic River and the Bergen County boundary on the east. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 21 degrees, so that north lies toward the upper left; the compass rose is at the left. The upper and middle blocks, along Stephens, Ralph, Davidson and Raymond streets and Bella Vista Avenue, are closely built with rows of small frame dwellings, many with garages, with a few brick-veneered and fire-resistive buildings and a school-sized building near the top of Ralph Street. Little and Terry streets cross the district; Mansion Place and several streets on the west edge are marked not opened. Along the river a strip is lettered Essex County Park Commission land. The L. J. Frebel Sons Company leather works stands at the end of Bella Vista Avenue near Main Street. South of Terry Street the sheet is given over to two large plants: the Eastwood-Nealley Corporation, makers of wire cloth and special valves, fills the blocks between Stephens Street and Main Street with wire weaving, wire drawing, machine and boiler buildings, and the American Dyewood Company, makers of black iron liquor and aniline dyes, occupies the ground east of Main Street with dye houses, a research laboratory and a coal yard. Water mains, hydrants, a fire alarm box and block numbers are shown, and the river is crossed by the boundary of the Borough of North Arlington, with the map of Harrison-Kearny noted beyond it.
notes: Bella Vista Avenue is Bellavista Avenue today; Ralph, Raymond, Little, Davidson, Main, Terry, Stephens and Joralemon are Ralph Street, Raymond Street, Little Street, Davidson Street, Main Street, Terry Street, Stephens Street and Joralemon Street.

sheet-32-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 32 is the main map, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 39 degrees with north toward the upper left. It shows the Silver Lake district on the Bloomfield line, almost entirely occupied by the plant of Thomas A. Edison Inc.: the Primary Battery Division, the Active Material Division chemical plant and the E. K. Medical Gas Laboratories. The works lie between Franklin on the north and Alva on the south, with Belmont Avenue along the east side and the Bloomfield town limits running diagonally across the west. Dozens of numbered buildings are drawn with their construction and use: vulcanized fibre and box factory buildings, iron reduction and nickel sulphate buildings, the nickel hydrate building, a carton storage, machine shop, battery assembling and shipping building, copper oxide building, caustic soda manufacturing, a power house, a sludge pond and a filter bed. The United Box and Lumber Co. yard adjoins on Belmont Avenue. A railroad yard with many sidings fans across the middle of the part. A few dwellings stand on Maioran Place, Franklin and along the north side of Alva near Edison. The plant's fire protection is summarised in a note at the lower left. Honiss, Jeraldo and Lawrence meet Belmont Avenue from the east; Florence Avenue, Frederick, Magnolia and Naples Avenue meet Franklin at the top. Part of the works is noted as also shown on the map of Bloomfield.
notes: Franklin is Franklin Street today; Magnolia is Magnolia Street.
The Edison works straddle the Belleville-Bloomfield line; the sheet notes the section is also shown on the map of Bloomfield.

sheet-32-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 32 lies to the right of the heavy dividing line and shows a separate area on the Newark city line, east of the main part, at the same scale of 100 feet to an inch and about the same orientation, with north toward the upper left. It covers the ground between Franklin on the north and Honiss and Monteith Avenue on the south, along Eugene Place and North 8th Street, with North 7th Street, marked not opened, running diagonally on the east. Heller Parkway meets Franklin at the top right. The part holds frame dwellings on narrow lots along Eugene Place and North 8th Street, a lumber yard with a lumber shed and a second-hand lumber building near the top, a few stores and a filling station on Franklin, and large vacant tracts (blocks 760, 761 and 763). The Belleville town limits and the City of Newark line cross the part, and buildings east of the line are noted as also shown in Newark volume three. An Erie Railroad line crosses the upper left corner. The rest of the right side of the sheet is blank, marked 'See Newark Volume Three'. Adjoining sheets are 36 to the north, 35 to the west and 33 to the south.

sheet-33.description: Sheet 33 shows a strip of south Belleville along the Newark city line, between Honiss Street at the top and Lawrence Street at the bottom. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 39 degrees, so that Belmont Avenue and Heckel Street run up the page; north lies toward the upper left. Belmont Avenue bounds the west side, with Heckel Street running parallel through the middle and Lake Street, continuing as North 10th Street, curving down the east side. Jeraldo Street crosses the sheet near the lower third, level on the west side of Heckel Street and bending upward to the right where it runs to the Newark line. The blocks west of Heckel Street hold detached frame dwellings with garages, Edison Playground and the Community House, and a large brick steam laundry with a second laundry shown as to be built. Along the lower left block are a motor freight terminal and a row of stores, storage and miscellaneous buildings. East of Heckel Street the blocks are mostly dwellings with a club, an apartment building and a few shops, and a strip of houses fronts the diagonal North 10th Street. The right side of the sheet is bounded by the Belleville-Newark town limits, drawn as a dash-dot line, with the words City of Newark and a note to see Newark Volume Three; buildings on the line are also shown in the Newark volume. The lower right has an open tract with the unbuilt line of Delavan Avenue and North 11th Street, and the compass rose. Water mains and fire alarm boxes are marked in the streets. Adjoining sheets are 35 to the north, 34 to the south and 32 to the west.
notes: Honiss, Heckel, Jeraldo, Lawrence and Lake are Honiss Street, Heckel Street, Jeraldo Street, Lawrence Street and Lake Street today.
Belmont Avenue keeps its name today.

sheet-34.description: Sheet 34 covers the southern tip of Belleville where Belmont Avenue and Heckel Street meet Bloomfield Avenue at the Newark city line. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 39 degrees, so the streets run up the page and north lies toward the upper left. Lawrence Street crosses the top, Alva Street enters at the upper left, and Bloomfield Avenue, a wide street carrying several water mains including the City of Newark supply, cuts diagonally across the bottom. Belmont Avenue and Heckel Street enclose a long block of dwellings, stables and small shops, with the D'Avella Macaroni Co factory, standing near its middle and a narrow diagonal lot line running down through the block. West of Belmont Avenue a strip of houses, a church and apartments lies along the town limits, the dash-dot line with Bloomfield to the west; a note says buildings on that line are also shown in the Map of Bloomfield and the area beyond is left blank. East of Heckel Street the blocks are bounded by Brook Street and Togo Place, with a junk yard, a metal foundry, iron works, a club and dwellings, and the right-hand edge is the City of Newark boundary, with a note to see Newark Volume Three. At the bottom, Chester Avenue, North 15th Street and North 13th Street appear in the Bloomfield and Newark margins. Fire alarm boxes and 6-inch water mains are marked throughout. Adjoining sheets are 33 to the north, 32 to the west.

sheet-35.description: Sheet 35 shows three blocks of the Silver Lake district of Belleville, bounded on the west by Honiss Street and on the east by Franklin Street. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 50 degrees, so the cross streets run across the page and north lies toward the upper right. Belmont Avenue crosses the top, Heckel Street and Lake Street follow below it, and Eugene Place runs along the bottom; Sheet 32 occupies the blank margins above and below. A pair of railroad tracks, lettered as the Erie Railroad Watchung Branch with the Silver Lake Passenger Station, runs diagonally from the upper middle to the lower right and cuts across the corner of the first block. Most of the sheet is detached frame dwellings with garages, lined up along the streets with their lot lines and house numbers; the block between Heckel and Lake Streets carries a row of stores and shops along Heckel Street and a large hall of fireproof construction near Franklin Street, and the block between Lake Street and Eugene Place holds St. Anthony of Padua R.C. Church with a chapel at its east end. A fire alarm box stands near Heckel Street and Franklin Street. East of Franklin Street the drawing shows only the heads of North Belmont Avenue, North 9th Street, North 8th Street and Watchung Avenue, which lie on Sheet 36. Water mains of 6 inches are marked in Honiss and Franklin Streets. Adjoining sheets are 33 to the west, 32 above and below, and 36 to the east.

sheet-36.description: Sheet 36 covers part of the Silver Lake district of Belleville, between Magnolia Street at the top and North 8th Street at the bottom, with Franklin Street along the left edge and the Newark city line at the lower right. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 48 degrees, so the cross streets run across the page and north lies toward the upper right. North Belmont Avenue and Watchung Avenue cross the sheet, and Cross Street runs down the right side, jogging at Magnolia Street. The top block between Magnolia Street and North Belmont Avenue holds Belleville Public School No. 4, a fireproof building shown in three sections with its dates of construction, flanked by rows of frame dwellings and stores along Franklin Street, and a junk yard and paper stock buildings near Cross Street. The block between North Belmont Avenue and Watchung Avenue is mostly dwellings, with a paper stock warehouse and a temporary paper storage building. South of Watchung Avenue the land is laid out in narrow lots, mostly vacant, with a few houses and a dairy near the town limits; the unopened lines of Cross Street and North 9th Street are marked not opened. The double track of the Erie Railroad Watchung Branch sweeps diagonally from the left edge to the lower right, with blocks of dwellings and apartments between it and Franklin Street. The right edge is the boundary with the City of Newark, with a note to see Newark Volume Three. Sheet 37 adjoins at the top and right and Sheet 32 at the lower left. Water mains of 6 inches and fire alarm boxes are marked.

sheet-37.description: Sheet 37 covers a district of northwest Belleville between Franklin Street on the west and Newark Avenue on the east, from Watsessing Avenue and the Bloomfield town line at the top to Watchung Avenue and the Newark line at the bottom. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 50 degrees, so Newark Avenue runs up the page and north lies toward the upper right. The cross streets, Salter Place, Naples Avenue, Florence Avenue, Frederick Street, Magnolia Street and North Belmont Avenue, run across the sheet at regular intervals, and Cross Street crosses the lower blocks with a jog at Magnolia Street. Franklin Street, a diagonal avenue lined with a row of dwellings, stores and shops, forms the left boundary. The blocks are largely built up with frame dwellings and garages, with a filling station on Franklin Street near Naples Avenue, the First Italian Baptist Church and a hall with club rooms near Maioran Place, and the Belleville Fire Department No. 3 at the foot of Franklin Street. The northeast corner is crossed by a dash-dot town line with a note that buildings on it are also shown in the Map of Bloomfield. The lower blocks around North Belmont Avenue and Cross Street contain houses, a junk yard and a few commercial buildings, and the bottom edge is the City of Newark line with a note to see Newark Volume Three. The right margin shows the heads of Brighton Avenue, Cuzzo and Rocco Streets across Newark Avenue. The area at lower left is left blank and labelled Sheet 36. sheet-38.description: Sheet 38 covers the northwest corner of Belleville along the Bloomfield and Newark town lines. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 51 degrees, so Newark Avenue runs up the page along the left edge and north lies toward the upper right. The upper third is a built-up district of frame dwellings between Harrison Street at the top, Watsessing Avenue and Brighton Avenue, crossed by Sanford Avenue and Wallace Street; the diagonal Bloomfield town line runs across the top left with a note that buildings on it are also shown in the Map of Bloomfield, and the area above is left blank for that map. Sanford Avenue, Highland Avenue, Forest Avenue and Rocco Street carry scattered dwellings, a church near the top right and a few stores and shops along the lower end of Wallace Street. West of Sanford Avenue the blocks between Newark Avenue and the line of Brighton Avenue are almost entirely vacant subdivision, drawn as long runs of narrow lots with a few new houses along Brighton Avenue. The lower two thirds is a platted but largely unbuilt tract: Newcomb Street, Kean (Athenia) Street and Whelan Street are lettered not opened, as are the lower stretches of Rocco, Frederick, Magnolia and North Belmont Avenue, and the only substantial building is a steam laundry in block 732 near Magnolia Street. A wide curving strip marked Abandoned Canal runs from the right edge down the sheet. The bottom is the City of Newark line, the former centre line of Meadow Brook, with a note to see Newark Volume Three. Sheet 37 adjoins on the left, Sheet 39 above and to the right and Sheet 40 at the lower right.

sheet-39.description: Sheet 39 covers the northwest corner of Belleville along the Bloomfield town line, which crosses the left side of the sheet as a dash-dot line with a note that buildings on that side are shown on the map of Bloomfield. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch. In the upper part, a row of detached frame dwellings fronts Smallwood Avenue, with Hewitt Place, Rhode Place and the unopened Lavergne street entering from the north, and a second row on the north side of Greenwood Lane at the left. The Erie Railroad Greenwood Lake Division runs across the sheet below them in a broad band of tracks, with the Belwood Park passenger station beside it, and Ricca Bros. coal yard stands at the right edge. A large tract of open land, numbered 590 and 520, lies between the railroad and the Second River, which curves across the middle of the sheet. South of the river, on Mill Street, stands the plant of the National Grain Yeast Corporation, a manufacturer of bakers yeast, drawn in colour with its sheds, boiler house and machine shop. East of it, Montgomery Public School No. 2 faces Mill Street. The lower half is a built-up residential district of one and two story frame dwellings on Harrison Street, Bellevue Avenue, Brighton Avenue, Maple Avenue, Montgomery Place and Acme Street, ending at Wallace Street and Oakwood Avenue, below which sheet 38 continues. An abandoned canal crosses diagonally north of Brighton Avenue. A hall with wood trusses stands on Harrison Street near Brighton Avenue. Adjoining sheets are 51 to the north, 40 to the east and 38 to the south.

sheet-40.description: Sheet 40 is mostly open ground at the east edge of the northern part of Belleville, along the Second River and the Newark city line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Only a narrow strip of built-up street at the left edge is drawn in detail: Mill Street crosses from the left to the works, and Montgomery Place runs down the margin with a row of small detached frame dwellings on its east side, continuing from sheet 39. The principal feature is the Belleville Copper Rolling Mills, a large plant drawn in colour beside the river, with rolling mills, a sheet mill, a rod mill and a coal-fired boiler house, and a watchman's clock-and-steam note for its fire protection. Mill Street runs to the plant and crosses the Second River on a bridge near the sheet number 41. East of the mills the river continues across the sheet through land marked as Essex County Park Commission property, and the city of Newark boundary follows Meadow Brook as a dash-dot line. Most of the right half of the sheet is blank, with notes directing the reader to Newark Volume Three and Volume Four, which cover the ground beyond the line. A small shed for offices and equipment stands in the open land south of the river. At the lower left an abandoned canal runs diagonally across the sheet, and stubs of Wallace Street, Sanford Avenue and Frederick are lettered at the border with sheet 38 below. Adjoining sheets are 39 to the west, 41 to the north-east and 38 to the south.

sheet-41.description: Sheet 41 covers the northeast part of Belleville along Belleville Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points toward the upper right. Belleville Avenue runs down the right edge of the sheet, with Carpenter Street, Cottage, Delavan Avenue, King Place and Walnut entering from the east side. At the top right, detached frame dwellings line Park Place and Lavergne, and Belleville Public School No. 10, built in 1926, stands on the avenue with a large coloured plan. Smallwood Avenue runs from the top centre down the left side of block 475 with a row of small frame houses, branching at Arthur Avenue, which is also lettered Hendricks Place, and a street lettered Copper (Arthur) Place meets Franklin Avenue near the Erie Railroad Greenwood Lake Division, whose tracks cross the sheet from the lower left to the upper centre. The Second River winds across the upper left past Montgomery Place, where Montgomery Presbyterian Church stands on a lot marked not opened, and then past the Belleville Copper Rolling Mills, drawn in colour on Mill Street at the left with a fire alarm box and a watchman's clock note. The lower two thirds of the sheet is open land of the Essex County Park Commission, including Hendricks Field Golf Course, crossed by the line of Delavan Avenue and several unopened streets. Adjoining sheets are 39 to the west, 40 to the north-west, 42 to the south, 49 and 52 to the east and 51 to the north.

sheet-42.description: Sheet 42 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right (about 57 degrees). Most of it is Belleville Park of the Essex County Park Commission, an open tract (blocks 320, 323, 395 and 396) crossed by the winding Mill road and by Park Drive, with the Second River flowing down the left side along the City of Newark town limits. A concrete foot bridge and a concrete bridge cross the river, and the Mount Prospect Avenue bridge carries a 30 inch City of Newark supply main at the bottom. Across the top lies the Hendricks Field Golf Course of the Essex County Park Commission, with a 36 inch City of Newark supply main running along its edge. Belleville Avenue runs down the right side, with Garden Avenue, Pleasant Avenue, Park View Avenue, Columbus Avenue, Cedar Hill Avenue and Mount Prospect Avenue meeting it from the east. In the lower right corner, between Parkside Drive and Union Avenue, is a small development of frame dwellings on Wilson Place, Parkside Drive and William, with several filling stations and a block of houses along Union Avenue near New. The ground left of the river is blank and marked 'See Newark Volume Four'. Adjoining sheets are 41 and 49 to the north, 47 to the east, and 43 and 45 to the south.

sheet-43.description: Sheet 43 covers a residential and mixed district of central Belleville between Union Avenue on the west and Bridge Street on the east, with William Street along the top edge and Mill Street near the bottom, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The sheet is turned about 25 degrees, with north toward the upper left. Smith and Clinton Streets run through the middle between the two cross streets, and Union Terrace and Wilson Place enter Union Avenue from the east and west. The blocks are filled with detached frame dwellings of one to two and a half stories, many with small rear garages, along with a number of tile and brick-veneered houses; larger buildings include a row of apartments at the north end of Union Avenue and the Municipal Welfare Department building with its offices and stores near Union Terrace, drawn in colour. A brick building with a coloured plan stands at the corner of Union Avenue and Mill Street. Water pipe sizes and hydrants are marked in the streets, with notes on the City of Newark supply mains beside Mill Street and Clinton Street. South of Mill Street the ground is open land of the Essex County Park Commission, bounded by the Second River, which also marks the town limit with the City of Newark; Mount Prospect Avenue and Summer Avenue cross the river on bridges at the lower left and lower right. A note across the bottom directs the reader to Newark Volume Four for the ground beyond the river. Adjoining sheets are 42 to the west, 45 to the north and 44 to the east.

sheet-44.description: Sheet 44 covers the area east of Bridge Street in central Belleville, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 25 degrees, with north toward the upper left. William Street crosses the top of the sheet, Church Terrace runs across the middle and Mill Street along the bottom, with Bridge Street on the left and Dow Street on the right edge; Van Rennsselaer, Cleveland, Howard Place and Clark enter from the east. The upper centre is occupied by the grounds of Saint Peter's Roman Catholic Church, whose large church building is drawn in colour with a cemetery lettered across the open ground to its west, and a rectory or school building beside it. The built-up area lies along Bridge Street at the left, where a row of detached frame dwellings and a stone-fronted building stand at the corner of Mill Street, and in the blocks between Church Terrace and Mill Street, with similar frame houses and garages around the numbered blocks 180 and 182. The right edge shows the sides of Dow Street lined with frame dwellings. At the bottom the Second River crosses the sheet through land of the Essex County Park Commission, lettered Belleville Park, and the dash-dot line along it is the boundary with the City of Newark; Bridge crosses it on a stone bridge at the lower left. Hydrants, fire alarm boxes and water pipe sizes are marked in the streets, with a note of the City of Newark supply beside Bridge Street. Adjoining sheets are 43 to the west, 45 to the north and 3 to the east.

sheet-45.description: Sheet 45 covers a compact district of central Belleville between William Street on the west and Belleville Avenue on the east, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points toward the right. Union Avenue crosses the top of the sheet and Dow Street the bottom, with Smith Street, Clinton Street and Bridge Street running across the middle between William Street and Belleville Avenue. De Witt Avenue, Prospect Place and Hornblower Avenue enter Belleville Avenue from the east. The blocks are filled with detached frame dwellings of one and two and a half stories with rear garages, numbered blocks 249, 252 and 186. At the right end of Smith Street, near Belleville Avenue, a group of stores and dwellings is drawn in colour, with a filling station beside it. Saint Peter's Parochial School, a large brick building with a class-room and auditorium plan and an additional wing with boiler room, stands in the lower left, and a convent lies along William Street near Bridge Street. A City of Newark water supply main of 24 inches is marked along William Street, Clinton Street and De Witt Avenue, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes in the streets. Adjoining sheets are 43 to the south-west, 44 to the west, 42 to the north, 46 to the east and 6 and 8 along the right edge.
