sheet-46.description: Sheet 46 covers the north-west corner of Belleville, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 76 degrees, so that north lies toward the right of the page. Joralemon runs diagonally up the left side from the bottom corner at Union Avenue to Garden Avenue at the top, and Union Avenue forms the bottom edge. Between them lie closely built blocks 279 to 282 and 360, cut by New, Van Reyper Place, Reservoir Place and Mertz Avenue, which run from Joralemon toward Division Avenue. Division Avenue curves up the right-hand side to Garden Avenue, and Belmohr, Forest, Adelaide, Tappan Avenue and Malone Avenue serve the dwellings of blocks 280, 289, 361 and 364 on the east side. The housing is almost wholly detached frame dwellings with garages in the rear; a large brick apartment group stands at the corner of Joralemon and Union Avenue, and a gas filling station and a small building stand on the east side of Tappan Avenue near Union Avenue. The upper part of the sheet is open land in blocks 362 and 405, with a cluster of outbuildings and sheds, and Princeton Terrace is drawn along the top as an unpaved street with a few houses. Water pipes of six, twelve, sixteen and thirty inch diameter are marked along Joralemon and Union Avenue. Adjoining sheets are 50 at the top left, 57 at the top right, 48 on the left, 58 on the right and 21 and 22 below.
notes: Mertz Avenue and Reservoir Place junctions with Joralemon and Division Avenue measured 6 to 10 m from their modern positions and were left out of the control.
Joralemon, Perry, New, Forest, Adelaide and Belmohr are Joralemon Street, Perry Street, New Street, Forest Street, Adelaide Street and Belmohr Street today.
Drawn scale (100 feet to an inch) agrees with the fitted scale.
NW Belleville, Joralemon / Union Av / Division Av; turned +76; Mertz Av and Reservoir Pl left out (6-10 m); 100 ft

sheet-47.description: Sheet 47 shows the middle of north-west Belleville around the Belleville Reservoir, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 76 degrees. Belleville Avenue forms the long diagonal left edge, Garden Avenue the top, Union Avenue the bottom and Holmes the right-hand edge. Between them the sheet is divided into rows of narrow blocks by Mount Pleasant Avenue, Park View Avenue, Columbus Avenue, Cedar Hill Avenue, Mount Prospect Avenue and New, which run from Belleville Avenue toward Maier and Holmes. Maier is drawn as two separate stretches, one in the upper blocks 340 and 341 and one in blocks 263 to 269, with Leslie Terrace and Crescent Terrace as short side streets. The blocks facing Belleville Avenue are mostly detached frame dwellings with small garages, with some stores, a filling station, a club and several apartment buildings along the avenue itself. The middle of the sheet, block 335, is the City of Newark Belleville Reservoir property and is left blank apart from its name. At the bottom Belleville Public School No. 8 stands in block 260 with an athletic field and grandstand beside Holmes, and a small cluster of stores and dwellings occupies the lower left corner. Water pipes of six, thirty and larger diameter, including a City of Newark supply main, are marked in the streets. Adjoining sheets are 49 above, 42 on the left, 48 on the right and 5 and 6 below.
notes: Maier is Maier Street today; Holmes and New are Holmes Street and New Street.
Park View Avenue is Parkview Avenue today.
The junction of Maier and Parkview Avenue is not drawn as a through junction on the sheet and was left out of the control.
Belleville Reservoir district, Belleville Av to Holmes; turned +76; 100 ft

sheet-48.description: Sheet 48 covers the east side of the Belleville Reservoir district in north-west Belleville, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 74 degrees. The Belleville Reservoir, 16,000,000 gallons capacity, fills the centre of the sheet inside block 345, marked as property of the City of Newark and crossed by large water conduits. Joralemon forms the curved right-hand edge from Union Avenue at the bottom to Garden Avenue at the top right, where the Town of Belleville Recreation Center stands, and Holmes forms the left edge. In the lower half, Cedar Hill Avenue, New and Union Avenue cross blocks 273 to 275 filled with detached frame dwellings, a few stores and a church or hall at the corner of Joralemon and Union Avenue. In the upper half, Garden Avenue, Perry, Dawson and Crescent Terrace serve blocks 350 and 352, which are built up with one and two family houses, and several streets run off the top edge, among them Hunkele, Minker Place and Springer. Pipe lines of six inch and larger mains, including the City of Newark supply conduits, are marked in the streets and across the reservoir grounds. A key line marks the edge of sheet 47 on the left, and Columbus Avenue and Mount Prospect Avenue are lettered where they meet the left edge. Adjoining sheets are 49 above, 46 on the right, 50 at the upper right and 13 below.
notes: Hunkele, Springer, Dawson, Holmes, Perry and New are Hunkele Street, Springer Street, Dawson Street, Holmes Street, Perry Street and New Street today.

Joralemon junctions with Van Reyper Place, Reservoir Place, Mertz Avenue and Perry Street measured 4.5 to 7.5 m from their modern positions, with water mains drawn in the street, and were left out of the control.
The placement rests on 7 control points and is of medium confidence.
east of the reservoir, Joralemon / Holmes / Garden Av; turned +74; Joralemon junctions with water mains excluded; 100 ft

sheet-49.description: Sheet 49 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right (about 60 degrees). Most of it is open ground belonging to the Essex County Park Commission and lettered Hendricks Field Golf Course, block 480 and part of block 402, with a brook winding across the top beside Franklin Avenue, a wide curving road in the upper part of the sheet. Belleville Avenue runs down the left edge. At the upper left it forks with Franklin Avenue, where Arthur Avenue also meets it, and a fire alarm box stands at the fork. The built-up part lies in the lower left: blocks 446, 447, 450, 452, 403 and 401 between Belleville Avenue and Jerome Avenue, cut by Cottage (marked not opened), Delavan Avenue, King Place and Walnut, with frame dwellings on narrow lots and a 6 inch water main along most streets. Garden Avenue crosses the bottom of the sheet from the lower left towards the right, with Maier meeting it from the south. A second group of dwellings at the right, blocks 353 and 445, lies along Fairview Place, Baldwin Place and Hunkele, with another street marked not named. The right edge carries the dash-dot match line to sheet 50. The sheets adjoining this one are numbered 41 and 42 on the left, 47 and 48 below and 52 above. The compass and the sheet number 49 stand in the top left corner.
notes: Cottage is marked not opened on the sheet; it was not used for control.
Walnut is Walnut Street today.
The Garden Avenue / Hunkele Street and Baldwin Place / Hunkele Street junctions carry residuals of 3 to 4 m, which may reflect parcel centres or narrower old streets.
golf course (Hendricks Field, Essex County Park Comm.); Belleville Av, Delavan, Jerome, King Pl, Walnut, Garden, Hunkele; 100 ft

sheet-50.description: Sheet 50 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right (about 60 degrees). Its centre is open ground of the Essex County Park Commission lettered Hendricks Field Golf Course, blocks 490 and 459, crossed by a brook; the dash-dot line along the left edge is the match line to sheet 49. Three built-up groups ring the open ground. At the top centre a small group of frame dwellings (blocks 556, 492, 495 and 491) lies along Arthur, Charles, Center, Irving and May, below Franklin Avenue at the upper left. At the right a strip of dwellings, block 465, fronts May, Passaic Avenue and Joralemon, with brick buildings (coloured pink) at the corner of Passaic Avenue and Joralemon, and Delia Terrace branches off May above it. Joralemon runs down the right side of the sheet towards the bottom, past block 407, with Princeton Terrace and Yale Terrace entering it from the east. At the lower left are blocks 354 to 356, 455, 457 and 458 along Fairview Place, Baldwin Place, Dawson, Minker Place and Springer, with Garden Avenue along the bottom edge; Springer is marked not opened in the lower part. The sheet number 50 and its references (62-63, Essex Co. Vol. 1) are at the top right beside the compass. Neighbouring sheets are numbered 52 and 55 above and to the right, 49 on the left, 46 and 48 below and 57 beyond Joralemon.
notes: Springer is lettered Springer (Fairview Pl.) in the upper part and Springer, not opened, below; the modern street is Springer Street.
Arthur, Charles, Center, Irving and May are Arthur Street, Charles Street, Center Street, Irving Street and May Street today; S. Wilber is South Wilber Street.
Upper cluster (Arthur, Charles, Center, Irving) junctions carry 3 to 4 m residuals and were measured from narrow street pairs; the streets are drawn about 40 ft wide against 50 ft in the parcels.
Dawson, Baldwin Pl, Minker Pl, Fairview Pl, Garden Av, Arthur, Charles, Center, Irving, May, Passaic Av, Joralemon; 100 ft

sheet-51.description: Sheet 51 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north about 8 degrees to the right of straight up. It covers the western edge of Belleville against the town line of Bloomfield, which crosses the left side of the sheet as a dash-dot line and is lettered Town of Bloomfield, with a note to see the Map of Bloomfield beyond it. The upper part is open ground of the Forest Hill Field Club, lettered as a golf course, with block 625 and block 607 left blank. A single row of narrow lots on the west side of Fairway, blocks 615 and 601, runs down the right of the sheet from Continenal Avenue at the top, with frame dwellings and a few outbuildings. The built-up district lies below the middle: Belleville Avenue crosses it diagonally from the upper left to the lower right, with Smallwood Avenue, Pleasant Avenue, Ogden Road, Stevens Road, Elena Place, Hewitt Avenue and Hewitt Place branching from it and many curved corners, in blocks 595 to 597, 605 to 609, 530 and 531. Houses are almost all frame, with a few brick buildings (coloured pink) and a fire alarm box near Hewitt. Rhode Place and Lavergne enter from the lower right, where the sheet meets sheet 41 at the bottom right corner. Sheet 53 adjoins the top, 52 the right, 39 the lower middle and 41 at the lower right. The compass and the sheet number 51 are at the top left.
notes: Continenal Avenue is printed so; the modern street is Continental Avenue.
Hewitt is lettered Hewitt Av. (Pl.) on one street and Hewitt Pl. (Av.) on another; the modern name is Hewitt Avenue.
Pleasant Avenue is lettered Pleasant Av. (Smallwood Av.).
Elena Place, Ogden Road, Stevens Road and Belleville Avenue keep their names; Lavergne is Lavergne Street and Rhode Place keeps its name.

Smallwood Avenue, Rhode Place and the Belleville Avenue junctions with Smallwood and Fairway were left out of the control: their modern lines carried residuals of 5 to 14 m against the drawn streets, which are curved and drawn differently today.
The control points all lie in the middle and south of the sheet except Continental Avenue / Fairway Avenue at the top, so the part north of the housing is extrapolated.
Continental Av (printed Continenal), Fairway Av, Belleville Av, Ogden Rd, Stevens Rd, Elena Pl, Hewitt Av; Smallwood Av and Rhode Pl left out (5-14 m); 100 ft

sheet-52.description: Sheet 52 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north about 8 degrees to the right of straight up. The left third is a long strip of narrow house lots along Fairway Avenue, blocks 615 and 600, running from Continental Avenue at the top to Belleville Avenue at the bottom, with frame dwellings facing the street and small outbuildings at the back; Carpenter bounds the strip on its east side. Across the top, Continental Avenue and Berkeley Avenue cross the sheet from Fairway Avenue towards the right, with Celia Terrace running between them past blocks 552 and 551 and a row of dwellings along Berkeley Avenue. The middle and lower part is the Essex County Hospital for Contagious Diseases, block 550 and block 540, drawn on a large scale in brown and pink with its named buildings: an Emergency Hospital, Mixed Infection Building, three pavilions, a laundry and central heating plant, the Student Nurses Home and Graduate Nurses Home beside Carpenter, and an Administration Building with East Wing and West Wing hospital wards, built in 1931 of fireproof construction. Franklin Avenue curves along the right side of the hospital grounds and joins Belleville Avenue at the lower right. Belleville Avenue crosses the bottom of the sheet from left to right, where Lavergne meets it. Neighbouring sheets are numbered 53 above, 51 and 41 on the left and at the bottom, 55 and 50 on the right and 49 below Franklin Avenue.
notes: Celia Terrace, Berkeley Avenue, Fairway Avenue and Continental Avenue keep their names; Carpenter is Carpenter Street and Lavergne is Lavergne Street today.

Continental Avenue / Fairway Avenue and the Berkeley / Carpenter / Celia Terrace junctions fit the rest of the sheet to 1 to 4 m; Belleville Avenue / Fairway Avenue was not used (it did not agree with the fit).
Continental Av, Fairway Av, Carpenter, Celia Ter, Berkeley Av; Essex County Hospital for Contagious Diseases; Belleville/Fairway left out; 100 ft
placenames: Essex County Hospital for Contagious Diseases

sheet-53.description: Sheet 53 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the right (about 83 degrees), so the streets that run north and south on the ground run across the sheet. It is almost all open ground. The upper third is the Forest Hill Field Club golf course on the Bloomfield side of the town line, which crosses the top as a dash-dot line lettered Town of Bloomfield with a note to see the Map of Bloomfield; the golf course is lettered Forest Hill Field Club, Golf Course. The Third River enters at the top right, loops sharply twice and leaves at the lower right, its channel drawn in blue. Large blocks 625, 617, 635 and 560 are marked with number only and left blank except for a few houses along Continental at the left edge, where Fairway Avenue and Carpenter meet it, and a handful of dwellings on the edge of block 560 along Barnett La. Celia Terrace crosses the middle on a long bend. At the bottom, Franklin Avenue crosses the whole sheet from left to right and Joralemon rises from it to the right. The only closely built ground is block 576 at the lower right, a small group of long narrow lots between Hill and Liberty Avenue, with a few frame dwellings and one brick building. Grove meets Joralemon above it. The compass and the sheet number 53 are at the top left. Sheets 52, 55 and 54 adjoin it.
notes: Barnett Lane is Barnet Lane in the modern data. Continental, Carpenter, Joralemon, Grove and Hill are Continental Avenue, Carpenter Street, Joralemon Street, Grove Street and Hill Street today.
Celia Terrace is drawn here as a long bend; the modern street has the same name but was not used for control.
All six control points lie along the bottom third of the sheet; the open ground above them is placed by extrapolation, so the upper part is low confidence.
Continental, Franklin Av, Joralemon, Barnet Lane, Hill, Liberty Av, Grove; turned +83; points in bottom third only; 100 ft

sheet-54.description: Sheet 54 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right (about 75 degrees). It lies on the northern edge of Belleville against the towns of Bloomfield and Nutley, whose boundaries cross the top and right edges as dash-dot lines lettered Town of Bloomfield and See Map of Nutley-Glen Ridge, with a note that buildings on the line are also shown on that map. Most of the sheet is open land. The upper left is the Glendale Cemetery (lettered across block 645), with the Third River winding down the left edge and crossing the middle of the sheet; a raceway, a pond and a wooden bridge appear near the right edge where a road crosses the river, and a Public Service Electric and Gas Company transmission line runs obliquely across the sheet. Joralemon crosses the left side towards the lower left, and Rutan Place runs from it in a long straight line to the right. At the top right a block of narrow lots (blocks 680 to 684) is laid out along Hoover Avenue, Maple Avenue and Morse Place, all marked not opened. At the lower left, blocks 655 to 658 between Elm Place, Grove, Hill and Liberty Avenue are subdivided into long narrow lots with a few houses and a brick building. Franklin Avenue crosses the bottom, with Chestnut and Triton meeting it, and blocks 577 and 665 hold a row of frame dwellings and a farm group, a vegetable house, sheds and pump house with an estate lettered August Plenge Sr. in block 665. Sheets 53 and 56 adjoin it on the left and below.
notes: Hoover Avenue, Maple Avenue, Morse Place, Elm Place and Triton are marked not opened; Rutan Place is marked unpaved.
Chestnut, Joralemon, Grove and Hill are Chestnut Street, Joralemon Street, Grove Street and Hill Street today; Franklin Avenue and Liberty Avenue keep their names.

Only four control points were found, all in the lower left, and the fitted scale is 3 percent above the 100 ft sheets around it. The rest of the sheet is extrapolated, so treat the placement as low confidence.
Grove Street / Joralemon Street, one of the four points, lies at the far left margin of the sheet.
Franklin Av, Liberty Av, Hill, Grove, Chestnut; Glendale Cemetery, Third River; four points, low confidence; 100 ft

sheet-55.description: Sheet 55 covers the Joralemon and Liberty Avenue district of north-east Belleville, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 73 degrees. Joralemon runs down the middle of the sheet from Franklin Avenue at the top to Passaic Avenue at the bottom, and Liberty Avenue forms a straight edge on the right. Between them the closely platted blocks 570, 572, 574, 502, 498 and 499 are cut by Melwex, Ligham, Wilber and Jefferson and are lined mostly with detached frame dwellings and garages, with a few brick buildings, and Harvard Avenue is drawn as an unpaved street through block 498. West of Joralemon, Charles, Center and South Wilber run off to the left through blocks 555, 557, 501 and 500, and Arthur, Irving and May cross them near the left edge; the lots there are mainly unbuilt. Franklin Avenue runs along the top edge, with Continental Avenue and Berkeley Avenue meeting it at the upper left. Delia Terrace and block 496 at the bottom include a small plant of blue-coloured buildings and an apartment building, and Passaic Avenue and Division Avenue run diagonally across the lower corner past block 499 and the open land beyond. Six and eight inch water pipes are marked in nearly every street. Adjoining sheets are 52 and 53 above, 50 on the left and below, 56 on the right and 57 at the lower right.
notes: Charles, Center, Arthur, Irving, May, Wilber, Melwex, Ligham and Jefferson are Charles Street, Center Street, Arthur Street, Irving Street, May Street, Wilber Street, Melwex Street, Ligham Street and Jefferson Street today; South Wilber is South Wilber Street.
Harvard is Harvard Place today.
The junctions of Joralemon and Passaic Avenue (two nodes ten metres apart in OpenStreetMap) were left out of the control.
Joralemon / Liberty Av, Franklin Av to Passaic Av; turned +73; 100 ft

sheet-56.description: Sheet 56 covers the northern edge of Belleville, from Franklin Avenue at the top to Passaic Avenue at the bottom and from Liberty Avenue on the west to the Nutley and Glen Ridge boundary on the east. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 72 degrees, so that north lies toward the upper right; the compass rose is at the top. The west side holds residential blocks 571, 573 and 575 between Liberty Avenue and Chestnut Street, with rows of small frame dwellings and garages along Melwex, Ligham and Wilber streets; Wilber Street is marked not opened at its eastern end. Chestnut Street runs the length of the sheet. East of it lies a large open area, blocks 580 and 516, crossed diagonally by the Public Service Electric and Gas Company's high-tension transmission lines and by the pipe lines of the City of Newark, the North Jersey District Water Supply Commission and the Passaic Valley Water Commission. The east side is built up along Hilton Street, Entwistle, Gless and Newark avenues, Moore Place and Memphis Avenue, with dwellings, a filling station and a few brick-veneered buildings, and the Nutley and Glen Ridge boundary is drawn along the right edge with a note that buildings on the line are also shown on the map of Nutley-Glen Ridge. Passaic Avenue crosses the lower part of the sheet, where Greylock Parkway, Greylock Place, Mitchell Street and Emmet Street meet it; the lower blocks are partly laid out in lots with few buildings. Water pipes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked, and the neighbouring sheets are numbered 54, 55, 57 and 59.
notes: Ligham is Ligham Street today. Chestnut, Hilton, Melwex, Wilber, Mitchell and Emmet are Chestnut Street, Hilton Street, Melwex Street, Wilber Street, Mitchell Street and Emmet Street.
Greylock Parkway is the modern continuation of Chestnut Street south of Passaic Avenue.
Triton does not appear in the modern street network.

Entwistle Avenue meets Meacham at the edge of the sheet and the junction was not detected. Gless Avenue / Meacham was left out as 5 to 8 m off the fit, and Franklin Avenue / Hilton Street as about 5 m off.
Sheet fits to 2.5 m RMSE; residuals along Chestnut Street of 3 to 4 m suggest the drawn street is not exactly on the modern line.
Franklin Av to Passaic Av, Chestnut St; Nutley line right; turned +72; 100 ft

sheet-57.description: Sheet 57 covers the north-east edge of Belleville, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 18 degrees counterclockwise, so that north lies toward the upper left. Greylock Parkway runs along the top, Nolton along the right edge, and Passaic Avenue runs down the left side, bending to the south-east where it meets Division Avenue, which crosses the sheet diagonally to Nolton. Joralemon forms the lower left edge, and Yale Terrace and Princeton Terrace run off it toward the bottom. The sheet is mostly open land: large vacant tracts 415, 382, 373 and 406 are cut by unopened streets, among them Hauck, Elm, Overlook Avenue, Tiona Avenue and a road marked not opened, and several of these are shown only as paper streets. Settlement is confined to the Passaic Avenue and Joralemon frontages, where detached dwellings and a few farm buildings stand, and to Belleville Public School No. 7, a large brick school with a yard, at the corner of Passaic Avenue and Joralemon. A large yellow building stands in block 466 behind Division Avenue. The Passaic Valley Water Commission and North Jersey District Water Supply Commission conduits, and those of the City of Newark, cross the lower right as three parallel lines. Adjoining sheets are 59 above, 56 and 55 on the left, 58 on the right and 50 and 46 below.
notes: Austin, Elm and Nolton are Austin Street, Elm Street and Nolton Street today.
Several streets (Hauck, Elm, Overlook Avenue, Tiona Avenue and the unnamed road) are marked not opened.
Passaic Avenue has two stretches side by side in OpenStreetMap; its junctions were checked and the placement is of low confidence (9 control points, leave-one-out 5.7 m).
NE edge: Passaic Av / Division Av / Nolton, mostly open land; turned -18; low confidence; 100 ft

sheet-58.description: Sheet 58 covers a closely built residential district of central Belleville, from Greylock Parkway at the top to Malone Avenue and Division Avenue at the bottom, and from Nolton Street on the west to Union Avenue and the blocks beyond it on the east. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 18 degrees, so that north lies toward the upper left; the compass rose is at the right. The blocks, numbered 290 to 302, 367 to 380 and 392, are laid out in a regular grid along Overlook Avenue, Tiona Avenue and Little Street, with Belmohr, Forest, Adelaide and Preston streets running down the page. Nearly every lot carries a detached frame dwelling with a rear garage; a few brick-veneered or fire-resistive buildings and several lines of dwellings marked as demolished appear along Nolton Street. Belleville Public School No. 5, a brick building with a frame addition, stands in the block bounded by Greylock Parkway, Forest Street and Overlook Avenue. Division Avenue cuts diagonally across the southwest corner, where the lots are irregular and the street is marked unpaved. The lower edge of the drawn area is Malone Avenue, beyond which the sheet is blank, and the ground south of it is shown on sheet 46. Agnes and Kathryn streets enter from the east edge beside blocks 24, 23 and 22 of neighbouring sheets. Fire alarm boxes, hydrants and six- and eight-inch water mains are marked along the streets. Adjoining sheets are 59 to the north, 57 to the west and 46 to the south.
notes: Little, Nolton, Belmohr, Forest, Adelaide, Preston, Kathryn and Agnes are Little Street, Nolton Street, Belmohr Street, Forest Street, Adelaide Street, Preston Street, Kathryn Street and Agnes Street today.
The modern junction of Forest Street and Overlook Avenue lies about 13 m from the drawn one and was not used as control.
Division Avenue at Nolton Street and Greylock Parkway at Nolton Street carry residuals of 5 to 6 m.
grid between Greylock Pkwy and Malone Av, Nolton to Union; turned -18; 100 ft

sheet-59.description: Sheet 59 covers the eastern edge of Belleville along the Nutley and Glen Ridge boundary, from Passaic Avenue and Memphis Avenue at the top to Union Avenue at the bottom, and from Greylock Parkway on the west to the boundary line on the east. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 72 degrees, so that north lies toward the upper right; the compass rose is on the right. The west side holds residential blocks 301, 313, 314, 377, 379 and 381 along Greylock Parkway, Belmohr, Forest, Adelaide, Campbell, Myrtle, Elmwood and Tremont streets and avenues, with detached frame dwellings, garages and several fire-resistive buildings; Nolton Street is marked not opened beside block 381. A wide band through the middle, blocks 426, 388 and 389, is open land crossed by the Public Service Electric and Gas Company's electric transmission lines, with Mary Street curving through it and only a few buildings. The upper blocks along Greylock Place, Austin and Mitchell streets and Passaic Avenue are partly built, and those along Emmet, Park, Federal and Jannarone streets and Memphis Avenue near the boundary hold small dwellings, a school-sized building and a church. The Nutley and Glen Ridge boundary runs down the right side with a note that buildings on the line are also shown on the map of Nutley-Glen Ridge. Union Avenue, with Sunset Avenue, Harvard Street and Yale Street, closes the lower edge. Adjoining sheets are 56 to the north, 57 and 58 to the west and 28 to the south.
notes: Austin, Mitchell, Emmet, Mary, Park, Federal, Jannarone, Nolton, Belmohr, Forest, Adelaide, Harvard and Yale are Austin Street, Mitchell Street, Emmet Street, Mary Street, Park Street, Federal Street, Jannarone Street, Nolton Street, Belmohr Street, Forest Street, Adelaide Street, Harvard Street and Yale Street today.
Hauck, Elm and Preston are lettered in the left margin, on streets that belong to the neighbouring sheets 57 and 58.
Mitchell Street / Passaic Avenue (6 m), Jannarone Street / Passaic Avenue (14 m) and Tremont Avenue / Union Avenue (15 m) were off the fit and were not used.
The top right (Memphis Avenue and Meacham Street) has no detected junction; it rests on the fit from the rest of the sheet.
Passaic Av to Union Av, Mary / Emmet streets, PSE&G transmission lines; turned +72; 100 ft
